content.title: About
content.content: Tomatoes, grape, raw (product code 5569) are small, round fruits that resemble grapes in shape but belong to the nightshade family. They have a sweet‑slightly tangy flavor and a juicy texture. Consumed raw, they are popular in salads, snacks, and fresh dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grape tomatoes are often called “cherry tomatoes” because of their tiny size.
They are rich in lycopene, which gives them a bright red color and provides antioxidant benefits.
Grape tomatoes can be grown in pots on a windowsill, making them a favorite of urban gardeners.
Their sugar content is higher than that of regular tomatoes, giving them extra sweetness.
In ancient Roman cuisine, small tomatoes were used in sauces and as garnish.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Grape tomatoes provide a good amount of vitamin C, supporting immune function and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of lycopene
items.content: Lycopene is a powerful antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative stress and supports heart health.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium aids in blood pressure regulation and normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: These tomatoes have low energy density, making them an excellent choice for weight management.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Nightshade allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, such as skin rashes or swelling.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: Unripe tomatoes contain small amounts of solanine, which can be toxic in large doses. Eat only fully ripe fruits.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Choose organic or thoroughly washed tomatoes to minimize exposure to pesticide residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Grape tomatoes can be eaten whole in salads, added to sandwiches, used in fresh salsas, side dishes, or as garnish. They also roast quickly on the grill or bake.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store grape tomatoes in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, in a paper bag or an open plastic container. At room temperature they keep for 2–3 days; refrigerated they last up to a week. Discard any fruit showing signs of spoilage.
